department: Department of Electronic, Electrical and Systems Engineering

deadline.value: General self-proposed research applications are considered on a rolling basis; advertised projects carry specific project deadlines.
deadline.quote: Make sure you read all the detailed information about the research project including duration, funding level/type, entry requirements and application deadlines.

entry_route.value: Applicants typically require a good Honours degree and usually a Master's degree (or international equivalent).
entry_route.quote: Once you have found your subject area you will need to check the entry requirements to see if you are eligible to undertake research with us. Typically you will need to have a good Honours degree and usually a Masters degree.

supervisor.value: Applicants proposing research must identify and contact a potential academic supervisor prior to formal application.
supervisor.quote: Once you've identified a subject area, you will need to find a supervisor for your project. All Doctoral Researchers are provided with a lead supervisor, who will act as the main source of academic supervisory support and research mentoring during your time as a Doctoral Researcher at the University.

funding.value: Funding is competitive and available via scholarships, research councils, charities, and loans.
funding.quote: To pay for your research, there’s a range of funding available from scholarships, charities, loans and self-finance.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: Postgraduate research programme (Electronic, Electrical and Systems Engineering PhD) in the Department of Electronic, Electrical and Systems Engineering at the University of Birmingham.
